analysis: Both units are BASE text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The file_changes patch excerpt is truncated and no head text is supplied, so I could not read the full change. The visible part of the change is documentation for a new repeatable `darkbloom sandbox setup --disk <volume>` option, which places the add-on's VM images and job data on operator-chosen volumes. The same PR also edits the Setup, Plan and Install steps and the status text near base lines 1100, 1155 and 1181, and head lines 1094-1109, 1117-1132 and 1249-1258, but I cannot see that content. The base text covers the unchanged contract: TB-013/T-061 (install.sh is run as the Mac owner and verified only by TLS and the 1 MiB, #!-shell checks), the owner-only add-on hold socket (TB-012), and the encrypted prefix cache on selected storage (T-041). No finding is reported, because no head-side line or behaviour was visible that regresses a control. Questions for integration or deeper review: (1) Does the Swift code behind `--disk` (SandboxCommand/SandboxSetupCommand, not in this batch) validate paths before passing them to the installer? That means making them absolute, rejecting option-like or odd values, and passing them as argv rather than through a shell. (2) Moving VM images and job data to removable or external volumes may need a TB-013/T-061 note. The note would cover ciphertext or plaintext retention, UUID cloning and denial of service, as already documented for T-041 cache volumes. (3) Does the 1.2.0 add-on installer trust anything extra from the `--disk` values? That is outside the supplied evidence and not verified. Nothing here changes the coordinator trust model, attestation or key custody.
